lines.text: Vera, I'm number 69. Does that mean “cat”?
lines.say: Vera, I'm number sixty-nine. Does that mean cat?

lines.text: Nothing. An ID is just a row number in a big learned table.
So what's in my row?
A long list of numbers: a vector. 768 in GPT-2 small, 12,288 in GPT-3.
lines.say: A long list of numbers: a vector. Seven sixty-eight in G P T 2 small, twelve thousand two eighty-eight in G P T 3.

lines.text: Who fills in all those numbers?
Nobody. Training nudges them, a little at a time.
Until tokens used in similar ways end up near each other.
So “cat” and “dog” end up neighbours, because they show up in similar sentences?
lines.say: So cat and dog end up neighbours, because they show up in similar sentences?

lines.text: Can I see that map?
The guide's toy: hand-built and flat, two numbers per word.
Look, the animals all huddle together!
And countries sit by their capitals. Related means close.
Type “cat” in the finder: its nearest neighbours light up.
lines.say: Type cat in the finder: its nearest neighbours light up.

lines.text: The surprise: directions mean something too.
Directions?
Start at king. Take away man, add woman.
And we land on… queen!
Real arithmetic. Man to woman is the same step as king to queen.
Is a real map flat like this?
No: hundreds or thousands of dimensions. And a direction rarely means just one human idea.
But close still means similar?
Yes. Similarity is a dot product: multiply matching numbers and add.
That dot product will become the heart of attention.
Can I try this myself?
Type a word into the finder in the Embeddings chapter, then build your own analogy.
Puppy minus dog plus cat… kitten! I'm a natural.
lines.say: Puppy minus dog plus cat... kitten! I'm a natural.
